title: Voicechain latency & cost snapshot
content:
Executive summary:

This is a quick, informal snapshot comparing three runtime configurations for a low-latency conversational/voice pipeline ("voicechain"):
  - baseline: full FP16 model (no kv-prefetch, conservative batching)
  - quantized: int8 static quant, same batching policy as baseline
  - prefetch-tiling: compact-context prefetch + small tiling window (aimed at high hit-rate for repeated short-turns)

Objective: capture p50/p90/p99 latency and unit token cost for a realistic short-turn voice workload (mean prompt+reply ~ 45 tokens), and highlight degenerate cases (microburst of 8 concurrent sessions each doing 3-5 turns in <10s).

Quick takeaway (TL;DR):
  - Quantized int8 lowers median latency modestly and reduces $/k token by ~22% on baseline under steady traffic.
  - Prefetch-tiling gives best p90 in conversational steady-state (cache hit helps) but suffers on cold-first-turn and when session churn is high; p99 can be worse than baseline during microbursts.
  - Under bursty short-turn patterns, the combination (quantized + prefetch) is promising but requires tuning of admission/slotization to avoid tail amplification.

Methodology notes (short):
  - Hardware: 2x A100-40GB (simulated multi-tenant on the same host), CUDA 11.8, driver 525.x
  - Model: 7B transformer, 2048 context, w/ KV cache enabled for tiled configs
  - Workload: synthetic voice-like traces derived from prod-telemetry (cohort: short-turns, mean tokens/request 12, response length 33)
  - Concurrency profile: steady (concurrency 48 sustained), microburst (8 sessions sudden fan-in; peak concurrency ~400 for 6s)
  - Cost calc: raw GPU compute time * local accounting rate (approx $2.40/hour per A100-40 for these estimates) + amortized infra charge. This is a simplified $/k token proxy used for relative comparisons only.

Raw numbers (representative sample run):

Latency (ms) p50 / p90 / p99  | baseline | quantized | prefetch-tiling
---------------------------------------------------------------
steady-state (sustained)      | 68 / 142 / 320 | 62 / 118 / 285 | 60 / 95 / 360
microburst (6s peak)          | 75 / 210 / 610 | 70 / 190 / 520 | 95 / 430 / 980
first-turn cold penalty       | 120 / 250 / 680 | 110 / 220 / 610 | 240 / 520 / 1200

Interpretation: quantized consistently trims medians and mid-percentiles. Prefetch-tiling reduces p90 in sustained conversation because KV cache hits remove decode and memory access for prefix frames; however warm-up/cold cases (and slot contention under microburst) can produce much larger p99s.

Unit cost sketch ($ per 1k tokens)
--------------------------------
Baseline: 0.72 $/k
Quantized: 0.56 $/k
Prefetch-tiling: 0.61 $/k (steady-state)
Prefetch under burst: effective $/k rises to 0.95 $/k when slot contention leads to retries and extended runtimes

ASCII sparkline of runtime distribution (p50..p99 relative scale)
(■ = relative weight at that latency bucket)
Baseline p95 slice:  ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ (p95 ~ 250ms)
Quantized p95 slice: ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ (p95 ~ 190ms)
Prefetch p95 slice: ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ (p95 ~ 330ms)

Operational annotations / TODOs:
  - Need a controlled run with mixed-precision quant (Q4 x8 hybrid) to see if tail improves vs int8 static (ENG-3421).
  - Re-run microburst with admission control toggled (slotization aggressive vs permissive) to capture tail sensitivity.
  - Add network variance (100ms p95 tail) to model edge cases for remote private deployments.
  - Verify accounting: current $/k uses host-allocated hour cost; will align with Product Optimize later for published collateral.

Notes on developer-facing collateral:
  - For a one-pager: highlight relative savings vs baseline at median + p90 chart; show a small callout about prefetch tail risk with guidance ("prefetch best for low-churn conversational customers; avoid as default for ephemeral bursty use-cases").
  - For console UI: include a toggleable view that shows steady vs burst-mode curves; allow customer to simulate their session churn (sliders: mean-turns, session-duration, concurrency spike factor).

Unresolved / open questions:
  - How sensitive is prefetch hit-rate to realistic user rewrites? Our synthetic traces assume repeated prompts that benefit from KV reuse; need to validate on natural-prod cohorts.
  - What admission policy (queue depth and fairness) minimizes p99 amplification when tiling is enabled? (Arjun to prototype in staging).
  - Is there a middle-ground quant profile that preserves p99 but gives most of the cost upside? (Liam to test mixed precision setups.)

    - p50 66ms, p90 145ms, p99 318ms, tokens 1.2M, runtime GPU-hours 0.94
  - quantized run id: run-20260329-14:18
    - p50 60ms, p90 119ms, p99 286ms, tokens 1.25M, runtime GPU-hours 0.72
  - prefetch run id: run-20260330-09:04
    - p50 59ms, p90 96ms, p99 367ms, tokens 1.18M, runtime GPU-hours 0.79
